title: "Create a DRAFT CapacityPlan and compute its shortage"
description: "Evaluates the ProcessPath path_id against assigned_demand (orders) for the warehouse's location over [window_start, window_end): loads each step's ProcessCapacity, normalizes it with the WorkloadProfile factors supplied in the body (same shape and validation as GET /process-paths/{id}/capacity -- there is no WorkloadProfile persistence yet), and computes path_capacity (ORDER per HOUR), bottleneck_step, capacity_over_window (path_capacity x window hours) and shortage (max(0, assigned_demand - capacity_over_window), never negative). The window is both the plan's planning window AND the window every step's ProcessCapacity is looked up for: a registered window applies to a step when it COVERS [window_start, window_end), exactly as in GET /process-paths/{id}/capacity (docs/adr/0003). The plan stores its own requested window. site_id is REQUIRED: the canonical site (a facility-layout Site site_code, the same identifier its SiteCapabilityChanged event publishes) the plan is scoped to. It is a stated planning fact, never inferred from warehouse_id or location, and a blank or absent one is rejected with 422 missing-required-field. assigned_demand is OPTIONAL (docs/adr/0004). An explicit value (including 0) is used exactly as stated and the plan's demand_source is 'request'. When it is OMITTED the demand defaults to the number of orders the local read model -- fed by order-management's published OrderAllocated / OrderPartiallyAllocated events, never by a live call -- expects at `location` in [window_start, window_end) (see GET /demand), the plan's demand_source is 'orders', and assigned_demand in the response is that figure. When the read model has no order for that location and window the request is rejected with 422 missing-assigned-demand: absence never silently means zero demand. The plan is saved and its CapacityPlanCreated event is queued in the transactional outbox in ONE database transaction."

>
</Heading>

<MethodEndpoint
  method={"post"}
  path={"/capacity-plans"}
  context={"endpoint"}
>
  
</MethodEndpoint>



Evaluates the ProcessPath path_id against assigned_demand (orders) for the warehouse's location over [window_start, window_end): loads each step's ProcessCapacity, normalizes it with the WorkloadProfile factors supplied in the body (same shape and validation as GET /process-paths/\{id\}/capacity -- there is no WorkloadProfile persistence yet), and computes path_capacity (ORDER per HOUR), bottleneck_step, capacity_over_window (path_capacity x window hours) and shortage (max(0, assigned_demand - capacity_over_window), never negative). The window is both the plan's planning window AND the window every step's ProcessCapacity is looked up for: a registered window applies to a step when it COVERS [window_start, window_end), exactly as in GET /process-paths/\{id\}/capacity (docs/adr/0003). The plan stores its own requested window. site_id is REQUIRED: the canonical site (a facility-layout Site site_code, the same identifier its SiteCapabilityChanged event publishes) the plan is scoped to. It is a stated planning fact, never inferred from warehouse_id or location, and a blank or absent one is rejected with 422 missing-required-field. assigned_demand is OPTIONAL (docs/adr/0004). An explicit value (including 0) is used exactly as stated and the plan's demand_source is "request". When it is OMITTED the demand defaults to the number of orders the local read model -- fed by order-management's published OrderAllocated / OrderPartiallyAllocated events, never by a live call -- expects at `location` in [window_start, window_end) (see GET /demand), the plan's demand_source is "orders", and assigned_demand in the response is that figure. When the read model has no order for that location and window the request is rejected with 422 missing-assigned-demand: absence never silently means zero demand. The plan is saved and its CapacityPlanCreated event is queued in the transactional outbox in ONE database transaction.
